body:
**WARNING: unreviewed LLM output**

## Goal
Reduce uncertainty for a Ymax vault spike by:
- specifying a concrete story + approach
- producing sequence/design artifacts
- implementing minimal contract-side Agoric wiring for creator-driven vault setup

## Included
- Story + evolving spike plan in `packages/portfolio-contract/.context-vaults/`
- Sequence/design docs in `packages/portfolio-contract/docs-design/`
- `creatorFacet.createVault(targetAllocation)` in portfolio contract
- target-allocation tests for creator-facet vault creation path

## Why this is a spike
This PR intentionally mixes design and minimal implementation to validate feasibility and identify risks quickly.

## Evidence / Outputs
- New creator-facet method returns `{ portfolioId, storagePath }` and starts portfolio open flow with fixed target allocation.
- Added tests in `packages/portfolio-contract/test/target-allocation.test.ts` for:
  - successful `creatorFacet.createVault(...)` publication path
  - invalid pool-key rejection

## Out of Scope
- production authority hardening and key custody
- full end-user vault UI
- full cross-chain integration smoke
- timer-driven periodic rebalance productionization

## Follow-up
Companion implementation/smoke PR in `agoric-labs/agoric-to-axelar-local` references this PR for EVM vault/factory + local smoke evidence.

## **User description** 🛡️ Sentinel Security Improvement **Vulnerability:** 1. **Missing Content Security Policy (CSP):** `apps/houselove` lacked a CSP, making it vulnerable to XSS and data injection attacks. 2. **Inline Script Execution:** The application relied on inline scripts in `index.html` to initialize EmailJS, which requires `unsafe-inline` and exposes configuration in the HTML source. **Fix:** 1. **Added CSP:** Implemented a Content Security Policy in `apps/houselove/public/index.html` that restricts script sources to `'self'`, `cdn.jsdelivr.net` (for existing dependencies), and allows necessary connections to `api.emailjs.com`. * *Note:* `'unsafe-inline'` and `'unsafe-eval'` are currently preserved to maintain compatibility with `react-scripts` (Create React App) development environment and potential runtime requirements, but the policy significantly reduces attack surface by restricting external domains. 2. **Refactored EmailJS Init:** Moved EmailJS initialization from an inline script in `index.html` to `apps/houselove/src/index.js` using the `@emailjs/browser` module. * This removes the need for the inline script. * It uses `process.env.REACT_APP_EMAILJS_PUBLIC_KEY` with the existing fallback to ensure no functionality is lost during the transition. **Verification:** - **Tests:** Ran `CI=true pnpm --filter house-love test` - All 14 tests passed. - **Dependency:** Confirmed `@emailjs/browser` is present in `package.json` and `node_modules`. - **Code Inspection:** Verified `src/index.js` imports `init` correctly and `public/index.html` has the correct meta tag and no inline scripts. - **Build:** Attempted build (`pnpm --filter house-love build`) failed due to pre-existing Tailwind CSS version conflicts in the monorepo (unrelated to these changes), but code logic is verified via tests. --- *PR created automatically by Jules for task [18429835095700872447](https://jules.google.com/task/18429835095700872447) started by @guitarbeat* ___ ## **CodeAnt-AI Description** Add Content Security Policy and move EmailJS initialization out of HTML ### What Changed - body:
### Problem

`SGXmlValidator.validateXmlFile` accesses `file.ast.component.children.children.flatMap(...)` without guarding against `children` being `undefined`. In BrighterScript's XML AST, `component.children` is only populated when the component XML actually declares a `<children>` block. Any component file without one (interface-only components, task nodes, etc.) causes a `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'children')` to be thrown inside `onFileValidate`.

BrighterScript's `PluginInterface` catches the unhandled exception and logs it to the console, but silently aborts validation for that file — meaning no diagnostics are produced for any component missing a `<children>` block, regardless of what other issues exist.

Discovered while integrating this plugin into [JellyRock](https://github.com/jellyrock/jellyrock) via Renovate ([jellyrock/jellyrock#347](https://github.com/jellyrock/jellyrock/pull/347)). JellyRock has ~170 XML component files, the majority of which have no `<children>` block, so every one was crashing the plugin silently.

author: copilot
body:
`ebitenmobile bind` was silently skipping Java compilation when run against NDK 26+, producing an AAR with only native `.so` files and no `classes.jar`. Gradle dutifully packaged the broken AAR into an APK, resulting in a `ClassNotFoundException: org.ebitengine.gomobile.GoNativeActivity` crash on every launch.

### Root causes fixed

- **NDK 26 toolchain path changes** break `gomobile`'s Java compilation step for Ebiten v2.9.x — cross-compilation succeeds but `classes.jar` is never written. Pinned to NDK `25.2.9519653`, the last release with stable support for this Ebiten version.
- **Stale `gomobile` cache** can trigger the same silent skip. Added `gomobile clean` before `gomobile init` in CI.
- **Missing `javac` preflight** in `build-android.sh` meant local builds would silently produce a `.so`-only AAR and only fail at runtime. Added hard fail on missing `javac` and warn on unset `JAVA_HOME` in `check_prerequisites`.

### AAR validation corrected

The existing validation was checking for `GoNativeActivity.class` — which is an Activity and belongs in the *app wrapper*, not in the *library* AAR that `ebitenmobile bind` produces. Replaced with checks for what the library AAR actually contains:

- `libgojni.so` (native bridge, per-ABI)
- `classes.jar` present in the archive
- At least one Ebiten bridge class (`EbitenView`, `EbitenSurfaceView`, or `Mobile`) inside `classes.jar`

The old check always evaluated as a false positive on a correctly built AAR, masking the real absence of `classes.jar`.

author: danmoseley
body:
When alternation branches are reduced to single nodes (e.g., `Set[Pp]` from a single-child Concatenation after prior prefix extraction), `ExtractCommonPrefixNode` previously bailed because it required all branches to be Concatenations. This caused IgnoreCase alternation prefix extraction to stop one character short (e.g., `htt` instead of `http` for `(http|https)`).

**Fix:** Remove the upfront gate check and handle both Concatenation and single-node branches throughout the extraction loop. When a single-node branch matches the common prefix, it is replaced with Empty.

Fixes #124871

**Tests:** 10 new test cases covering http/https IC, shorter-branch-is-prefix, multi-char difference, 3-branch variants, case-sensitive regression guard, behavioral match correctness, 4-branch mixed single-node/Concat, and non-IgnoreCase Set-node branches.

🛡️ Sentinel: [SECURITY ENHANCEMENT] Add security headers

**Vulnerability:** Missing security headers (HSTS, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy).
**Impact:** 
- Lack of HSTS allows downgrade attacks (HTTP instead of HTTPS).
- Missing Referrer-Policy can leak sensitive URL paths in Referer headers.
- Missing Permissions-Policy allows frames to potentially access sensitive features like microphone/camera without explicit restriction (though browser prompts still apply).

**Fix:** 
- Updated `transcription/service_middleware.py` to add:
    - `Strict-Transport-Security`
    - `Referrer-Policy`
    - `Permissions-Policy`
- Updated `tests/test_service.py` to verify these headers.

**Verification:**
- Ran `uv run --extra dev pytest tests/test_service.py` and all tests passed, including the new assertions.

## Motivation and Context

This PR introduces an automated documentation improvement workflow for the MSstatsBioNet R package. The goal is to leverage AI (specifically OpenAI's GPT-4) to systematically enhance roxygen2 documentation blocks for exported functions. The workflow is triggered on pull requests and can also be manually dispatched, randomly selecting one exported function per cycle to receive AI-assisted documentation improvements, which are then submitted as pull requests for human review and approval.

## Solution Summary

The implementation consists of three components:
1. A Python script that scans the R package for exported functions (those tagged with @export in roxygen2 blocks)
2. A Python script that calls the OpenAI API to improve the roxygen2 documentation for a selected function
3. A GitHub Actions workflow that orchestrates these scripts and creates pull requests with the documentation improvements

## Detailed Changes

- **`.github/scripts/pick_target.py`** (84 lines added)
  - Scans the `R/` directory for all R files
  - Identifies functions with `@export` tags in their preceding roxygen2 comment blocks
  - Supports both `<-` and `=` assignment operators for function definitions
  - Handles file-reading errors gracefully with per-file error messages
  - Randomly selects one function from the pool of exported candidates
  - Outputs the selected target to GitHub Actions `GITHUB_OUTPUT` for downstream workflow steps (or prints to stdout for local execution)
  - Exits with status code 1 if no exported functions are found

- **`.github/scripts/upgrade_docs.py`** (84 lines added)
  - Reads environment variables: `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `TARGET_FILE`, and `TARGET_FUNCTION`
  - Validates that all required environment variables are present before proceeding
  - Loads the target R file and constructs a detailed prompt for the OpenAI API
  - Calls OpenAI's GPT-4o model with a temperature of 0.3 for consistent output
  - Includes a comprehensive `PROMPT_TEMPLATE` constant that specifies:
    - Roxygen2 formatting rules and allowed tags (@description, @param, @return, @examples)
    - Parameter documentation format with type and description requirements
    - Requirement to preserve the @export tag
    - Instructions to only modify documentation, not code logic
  - Writes the AI-generated updated file content back to the target file
  - Provides status messages before and after the upgrade

- **`.github/workflows/weekly-doc-upgrade.yml`** (90 lines added)
  - Workflow named "Weekly AI Doc Upgrade"
  - Triggers on any pull request and manual dispatch via `workflow_dispatch`
  - Runs on `ubuntu-latest`
  - Execution steps:
    - Checks out the repository
    - Sets up Python 3.11
    - Installs the `openai` Python package via pip
    - Executes `pick_target.py` to select a random exported function
    - Executes `upgrade_docs.py` with environment variables including OpenAI API key and target information
    - Creates a new branch with naming pattern `ai-docs/YYYY-MM-DD-{FUNCTION_NAME}`
    - Commits the changes with descriptive commit message
    - Pushes the branch to origin
    - Creates a pull request using the GitHub CLI (`gh`) with:
      - Title: `docs: Weekly AI doc upgrade for {FUNCTION_NAME}`
      - Pre-populated body with checklist for reviewer validation
      - Labels: `documentation` and `automated`
      - Target: `main` branch
  - Includes setup instructions in comments for configuring GitHub Secrets and Actions permissions

## Unit Tests

No unit tests were added for the Python scripts in this PR. The repository contains an existing test suite for R code using the testthat framework (located in `tests/testthat/`), but there are no test files for the new Python automation scripts.

## Coding Guidelines

No coding guideline violations were identified. The repository does not have explicit Python coding standards configuration files (such as `.flake8`, `pyproject.toml`, or `.pylintrc`). The Python scripts follow standard conventions with:
- Clear function and variable naming
- Proper error handling and user-friendly error messages
- Environment variable validation
- Module-level docstrings
- Appropriate use of the standard Python main guard (`if __name__ == "__main__"`)
- Reasonable script structure and organization

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

author: re-bin
body:
## Summary

Allow users to explicitly select an LLM provider in `config.json` instead of relying solely on auto-detection.

Adds a `provider` field to `AgentDefaults` (default: `"auto"` for full backward compatibility).

## Motivation

When users configure API keys for multiple providers (e.g. both `anthropic` and `openrouter`), the current auto-detection logic picks the first match based on model name keywords and registry order. This makes it impossible to pin a specific provider — especially for gateway providers like OpenRouter that can serve any model name.

## Design

- **Minimal change**: 1 new field + 4 lines of logic in `_match_provider()`
- **Backward compatible**: `"auto"` (default) preserves the existing auto-detection behavior exactly
- **Fail-safe**: If the user types an invalid provider name, returns `(None, None)` — downstream reports "No API key configured" rather than silently falling back
- **No side effects**: Only affects LLM provider matching; independent paths like Groq voice transcription are untouched

## Usage

```json
"defaults": {
  "model": "claude-sonnet-4-6",
  "provider": "anthropic"
}
```

Valid provider names match `ProvidersConfig` attributes: `anthropic`, `openai`, `openrouter`, `deepseek`, `groq`, `gemini`, `openai_codex`, etc.

## Changed files

- `nanobot/config/schema.py` — add `provider` field to `AgentDefaults`; add early-return branch in `_match_provider()`

author: tootallnate
body:
## Summary

Fixes a bug where the `<Group>` component's backing canvas would use the HTML default size of 300×150 when `contentWidth` / `contentHeight` were explicitly set to `0` (e.g. on initial render before content loads).

## Problem

The `<Group>` component used `canvasW || 300` and `canvasH || 150` when creating the backing canvas, which treated an explicit `contentHeight={0}` the same as "not provided" — both fell back to 150px. The resize logic on subsequent renders also had a `canvasH > 0` guard that prevented resizing a canvas from the fallback size to a real value of `0`.

This caused a visible bug in apps that initialize with an empty list (e.g. `contentHeight={0}`) and then load data: the Group would render ~4 items worth of content (150px / item height) instead of nothing, and then fail to resize correctly when the real content height was set.

## Changes

### `@react-tela/core` (`packages/core/src/group.ts`)
- Use `typeof this.contentWidth === 'number'` instead of `!== undefined` for viewport mode detection — more explicit about the intent

### `react-tela` (`packages/react-tela/src/index.tsx`)
- Use `typeof props.contentHeight === 'number'` checks instead of `??` for determining canvas dimensions — clearly distinguishes "prop was provided with a numeric value (including 0)" from "prop was not provided"
- Remove the `|| 300` / `|| 150` fallbacks from canvas creation — the backing canvas now uses exact dimensions
- Remove the `> 0` guards from the canvas resize logic — always sync to current dimensions

### Tests (`packages/react-tela/test/group-viewport.test.tsx`)
Added 3 new test cases (6 including StrictMode variants):
- `should not use 300x150 default when dimensions are 0` — a 0×0 Group doesn't leak child content
- `should not use 300x150 default when contentHeight is 0` — `contentHeight={0}` produces no visible content
- `should render correctly when contentHeight changes from 0 to a real value` — canvas properly resizes when `contentHeight` transitions from 0 → real value via state update

### What does this PR do?

✅ User can add ClientSecret to appsettings.json and restart
✅ All configuration methods supported (appsettings.json, appsettings.Local.json, user secrets, environment variables)

1. Get ClientSecret from Azure Portal → Azure AD → App registrations → Certificates & secrets
2. Open `src/portal-blazor/SharePointExternalUserManager.Portal/appsettings.json`
3. Replace `"ClientSecret": ""` with your actual secret value

author: coderzc
body:
## Problem

When the .idxx index file is empty (0 bytes), `ReadIndex()` would panic with `slice bounds out of range [4:0]` when trying to read the CRC at offset 0.

Stack trace from #737:
```
github.com/streamnative/oxia/server/wal/codec.(*V2).ReadIndex
    /src/oxia/server/wal/codec/v2.go:189 +0x47d
```

## Solution

Added a length check before reading the index. If the file is shorter than the header size (4 bytes), it returns `ErrDataCorrupted` instead of panicking, allowing the caller (`readonly_segment.go`) to rebuild the index from the txn file.

## Changes

- `oxiad/dataserver/wal/codec/v2.go`: Added length check in `ReadIndex()`
- `oxiad/dataserver/wal/codec/v2_test.go`: Added tests for empty and short index files

## Test Plan

```bash
go test -v ./oxiad/dataserver/wal/codec/... -run "TestV2_ReadEmptyIndex|TestV2_ReadShortIndex"
```

Both tests pass:
- `TestV2_ReadEmptyIndex`: verifies empty file (0 bytes) returns `ErrDataCorrupted`
- `TestV2_ReadShortIndex`: verifies short file (<4 bytes) returns `ErrDataCorrupted`

Fixes #737

Bootstrap an empty repo into a production-ready Next.js 16 personal portfolio using the App Router, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS.

## Structure
- `app/page.tsx` — assembles all sections in order
- `app/layout.tsx` — root layout with SEO metadata
- `app/globals.css` — system font stack, Tailwind base, smooth scroll
- `app/components/` — one file per section:
  - `Navbar` — fixed, backdrop-blur, responsive with mobile hamburger
  - `Hero` — headline, subtitle, CTA buttons
  - `About` — bio, quick-info grid, CV download link
  - `Skills` — skills grouped by Frontend / Backend / Tools
  - `Projects` — card grid with tag pills, live demo + GitHub links
  - `Contact` — form (name/email/subject/message) + social icon links

- System fonts instead of Google Fonts — no external network requests at build time
- All sections are server components except `Navbar` (`"use client"` for menu toggle state)
- `tsconfig.json` uses `"jsx": "preserve"` — correct for Next.js (framework owns the transform)

Comprehensive security audit of the NATS server codebase identifying 10 vulnerabilities across authentication, protocol parsing, WebSocket handling, and monitoring endpoints.

### Key Findings

**High severity:**
- **JSONP callback injection (XSS)** — `monitor.go:2550-2555`: `callback` query param written directly into response body without sanitization
  ```go
  fmt.Fprintf(w, "%s(%s)", callback, data) // unsanitized user input
  ```
- **WebSocket frame size integer overflow** — `websocket.go:278`: `uint64` → `int` cast truncates on 32-bit, enabling DoS
- **Overly permissive CORS** — `monitor.go:2559`: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on all JSON monitoring responses enables cross-origin data exfiltration
- **`parseSize` integer overflow** — `util.go:102`: no overflow guard on multiplication, result used in `make([]byte, n)`
- **Username timing side-channel** — `auth.go:1134`: usernames compared with `!=` while passwords use `subtle.ConstantTimeCompare`

**Medium severity:**
- **JWT credential leakage** — `monitor.go:438`: `/connz?auth=true` returns full client JWTs on an unauthenticated endpoint
- ******** skips nonce verification** — `auth.go:994`: `BearerToken` flag bypasses nonce signature check entirely (note the existing `FIXME` comment)
- **Config parser stack exhaustion** — `conf/lex.go:143`: no depth limit on nested config structures

**Low severity:**
- TLS `InsecureSkipVerify` configurable without strong warnings
- Symlink following in JWT dir store file reads

### Deliverable

`SECURITY_AUDIT.md` — full report with code locations, CVSS ratings, PoC reproduction steps, and prioritized remediation guidance for each finding.

author: rotdrop
body:
… return from within an active transaction.

Why: the database connection is shared between all the code of the PHP script life-time. Opening another transaction from within an transaction is ok, but not committing that transaction is not ok as this will finally lead to a state where the script exits with positive transaction nesting level. This has the effect that ALL database mutations performed by ALL other modules (and also by the context_chat) module will just be discarded.

Thus, if any app does not properly commit all transaction frames it has started then "evil things" will happen ;)

author: alexander-acker
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces a new **Coeadapt channel** that integrates Open Cowork with the Coeadapt career development platform, enabling bi-directional messaging and career workflow automation. Users can now leverage AI agents for resume generation, skill gap analysis, portfolio creation, interview prep, and job search directly from their desktop while connected to Coeadapt.

## Key Changes

- **New Coeadapt Channel Implementation** (`src/main/remote/channels/coeadapt/`)
  - `coeadapt-channel.ts`: Main channel connector extending `ChannelBase` with WebSocket support, automatic reconnection with exponential backoff, and event handling
  - `coeadapt-api.ts`: REST/WebSocket API client with OAuth token management, credential refresh, and endpoints for user profiles, career tools, portfolio, and messaging
  - `index.ts`: Public exports for channel and API types

- **Type System Updates** (`src/main/remote/types.ts`)
  - Added `'coeadapt'` to `ChannelType` union
  - New `CoeadaptChannelConfig` interface with configuration for base URL, API key, OAuth, WebSocket endpoint, webhooks, user mapping strategy, and feature toggles (career sync, job search, interview prep, portfolio builder, skill tracking)
  - New `CoeadaptEventType` union for platform events (career roadmap updates, skill gap analysis, portfolio reviews, interview sessions, job matches, etc.)

- **Remote Manager Integration** (`src/main/remote/remote-manager.ts`)
  - Added `CoeadaptChannel` import and instantiation
  - New `updateCoeadaptConfig()` method to persist Coeadapt configuration

- **Configuration Store** (`src/main/remote/remote-config-store.ts`)
  - Added `getCoeadaptConfig()` and `setCoeadaptConfig()` methods for persisting Coeadapt settings

- **UI Configuration Panel** (`src/renderer/components/RemoteControlPanel.tsx`)
  - New Coeadapt configuration step with form fields for base URL, API key, and feature toggles
  - Added Briefcase icon for Coeadapt tab
  - Configuration state management and save/load logic

- **IPC Bridge Updates** (`src/preload/index.ts`, `src/main/index.ts`)
  - Exposed `updateCoeadaptConfig` IPC handler for renderer process

- **Career Skill Definition** (`.claude/skills/coeadapt-career/SKILL.md`)
  - New skill for career development workflows including resume builder, cover letter writer, portfolio generator, interview coach, skill gap analyzer, and job match evaluator

- **Launch Documentation** (`docs/COEADAPT_LAUNCH_MASTER_PLAN.md`)
  - Comprehensive integration strategy, architecture overview, implementation phases, technical specifications, security considerations, and success metrics

## Notable Implementation Details

- **WebSocket Reconnection**: Implements exponential backoff (2s–30s) with configurable reconnect delays for resilient real-time event handling
- **Token Management**: Automatic OAuth token refresh with deduplication of concurrent refresh calls
- **Event Mapping**: Converts Coeadapt platform events into `RemoteMessage` objects with contextual prompts for AI agent processing
- **Error Handling**: Retry logic with configurable max attempts and delays for API calls; graceful degradation on connection failures
- **Feature Toggles**: Granular control over integration capabilities (career sync, job search, interview prep, portfolio builder, skill tracking)
- **User Mapping Strategy**: Configurable user identification across platforms (email, Coeadapt ID, or custom)

## Integration Points

The Coeadapt channel integrates seamlessly with Open Cowork's existing remote control architecture:
- Extends `ChannelBase` for consistent channel lifecycle management
- Uses `RemoteMessage` and `RemoteResponse` for standardized message handling
- Leverages existing `withRetry` utility for resilient API calls
- Integrates with skill system for career document generation (resume, cover letter, portfolio case studies)

author: jmf-pobox
body:
## Summary

- Add `DisplayQueue` — a pure synchronous data structure that manages rotation of wall and talk items on the status bar. Wall items cycle indefinitely (15s per turn), talk items are shown once then discarded.
- Replace separate wall/talk status bar segments with a unified display pipeline: the queue determines what the human sees, while tool descriptions (for Claude) continue to show full state.
- Simplify the unread file schema from `wall`/`wall_from`/`talk_partner`/`talk_message` to `display_text`/`display_kind`.
- Net -55 lines. All quality gates pass (829 tests, 0 type errors).

### Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/biff/server/display_queue.py` | **New** — `DisplayItem` + `DisplayQueue` with rotation, dedup, force-to-front |
| `tests/test_server/test_display_queue.py` | **New** — 29 unit tests covering empty, add, remove, rotation, timing |
| `src/biff/server/state.py` | Add `display_queue` field to `ServerState` |
| `src/biff/server/tools/_descriptions.py` | Migrate wall/talk globals → queue items, add `_sync_unread_file`, rotation in `_active_tick` |
| `src/biff/statusline.py` | `_wall_segment` + `_talk_segment` → unified `_display_segment`, simplified `SessionUnread` |
| `tests/test_statusline.py` | Update for new schema and unified display segment |

## Test plan

- [x] 29 new unit tests for `DisplayQueue` (rotation, dedup, removal, timing, edge cases)
- [x] 101 statusline tests updated and passing
- [x] Full tier 1-2 suite: 829 passed
- [x] ruff check + format, mypy, pyright: zero issues
- [ ] Manual testing with live NATS (wall + talk rotation on real status bar)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches the live status bar/unread-file pipeline and changes the unread JSON schema, which could break existing consumers or regress rotation/notification timing despite good test coverage.
> 
> **Overview**
> Introduces a new synchronous `DisplayQueue` (and `DisplayItem`) on `ServerState` to rotate status bar line 2 content: **wall** items persist and cycle, while **talk** items are shown once then discarded (with new talk forced to the front and per-sender coalescing).
> 
> Reworks server description/unread-file updates to source status bar output from the queue via a new `_sync_unread_file`, rotates the queue on the poller tick, and clears talk items when the talk partner changes.
> 
> Updates the status line renderer and unread JSON schema from `wall`/`talk_*` fields to `display_text`/`display_kind`, replacing separate wall/talk rendering with a unified `_display_segment`; adds comprehensive unit tests for queue behavior and updates statusline tests accordingly.

author: edspencer
body:
## Summary

Fixes #149 - Catch-all 404 in `/by-path` route masks server errors

### Problem

The `/api/chat/sessions/by-path/:encodedPath/:sessionId` and `/api/chat/:agentName/sessions/:sessionId` routes were returning 404 for **all** exceptions, including:
- Permission errors (EACCES)
- Disk failures (EIO)
- Parse errors
- Any other server-side errors

This made it impossible for monitoring/alerting to distinguish "session doesn't exist" from "server can't read the filesystem."

### Solution

Both routes now return:
- **404** only for `ENOENT` (genuine "not found" cases when the session file doesn't exist)
- **500** for all other errors (permission denied, disk failures, parse errors, etc.)

This matches the error handling pattern already used in other routes (`/usage`, `/agent/sessions`) that correctly return 500 for server errors.

### Changes

- Modified catch blocks in two endpoints to check error code before determining HTTP status
- Added explicit `ENOENT` check for 404 responses
- All other errors now correctly return 500

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify existing tests pass (CI will run full test suite)
- [ ] Manually test: request a non-existent session → receives 404
- [ ] Manually test: simulate permission error → receives 500

body:
## Summary

Describe the problem and fix in 2–5 bullets:

- Problem: Discord voice messages (`asVoice: true`) always fail with a bare `"Error"` — no API status code, no stack trace, no indication of which step failed.
- Why it matters: Any Discord bot user sending voice messages gets an opaque failure with no actionable diagnostic; the feature is effectively broken.
- What changed: `sendDiscordVoiceMessage()` now uses a raw `fetch` call (with `Authorization: Bot <token>` header) for the upload-URL step only. On non-2xx it throws `DiscordError` or `RateLimitError` (matching Carbon semantics) so the retry runner and `buildDiscordSendError()` can classify errors correctly.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): Steps 2 (CDN PUT) and 3 (message POST) still use Carbon's `rest.post`. No other Discord send paths are affected; the token is threaded through only to this one call site.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #16103
- Related #19668

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

List user-visible changes (including defaults/config).  
If none, write `None`.

Discord voice messages (`asVoice: true`) now succeed instead of failing silently. When an error does occur, the error message contains the Discord API status code and error body (e.g. "Missing Access", code 50001) rather than a bare `"Error"`.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? Yes
- New/changed network calls? Yes
- Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- Data access scope changed? No
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: The bot token is now passed into `sendDiscordVoiceMessage()` and used in a single raw `fetch` `Authorization` header for the upload-URL step. The token was already available at the call site and already sent to Discord via Carbon for every other request — this change does not expand scope. The raw fetch call is scoped to a single internal step, not exposed to user-controlled input.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS / Linux
- Runtime/container: Node 22+
- Model/provider: any
- Integration/channel (if any): Discord
- Relevant config (redacted): Discord bot token + channel with `AttachFiles` + `SendMessages` permissions

### Steps

1. Configure a Discord bot account in OpenClaw.
2. Call the `message` tool with `asVoice: true` and a valid audio file path targeting a Discord channel.
3. Observe the result.

### Expected

- Voice message is delivered to the Discord channel as a native voice message (blue waveform player).

### Actual

- Tool returns `{"status": "error", "error": "Error"}` with no additional context.

## Evidence

Attach at least one:

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

New test file `src/discord/voice-message.upload-url.test.ts` (130 lines, 3 cases):
1. Confirms step 1 uses raw `fetch` with `Content-Type: application/json` and `Authorization: Bot <token>` headers (not Carbon's `rest.post`).
2. Confirms non-2xx throws `DiscordError` with structured Discord API body so `buildDiscordSendError` can classify it.
3. Confirms 429 throws `RateLimitError` so the retry runner can back off correctly.

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios: Unit tests pass; build and lint are clean; root cause confirmed by reading Carbon's `RequestClient.executeRequest` source.
- Edge cases checked: 403 (missing permissions), 429 (rate limit), successful round-trip through all three voice message steps.
- What you did **not** verify: End-to-end delivery on a live Discord bot (no live bot available in this environment).

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config/env changes? No
- Migration needed? No
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: Revert commit `c2996c6be`; the only production files changed are `src/discord/voice-message.ts` and `src/discord/send.outbound.ts`.
- Files/config to restore: `src/discord/voice-message.ts`, `src/discord/send.outbound.ts`
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: If `token` is undefined at the call site, the raw fetch will be sent without an `Authorization` header and receive a 401. The `DiscordError` throw path will surface this clearly rather than silently.

## Risks and Mitigations

List only real risks for this PR. Add/remove entries as needed. If none, write `None`.

- Risk: Raw `fetch` bypasses any future Carbon middleware (retry hooks, request logging) added to `rest.post`.
  - Mitigation: The retry runner (`request()`) still wraps the entire step; only the innermost HTTP call is raw. Carbon middleware for the other two steps is untouched.
- Risk: If a new call site calls `sendDiscordVoiceMessage()` without passing `token`, the upload-URL request will fail with a 401.
  - Mitigation: `token` is optional (`token?: string`); the function throws a clear `DiscordError` on 401 rather than a bare `Error`. The existing call site already has the token available and passes it correctly.

## Summary

Rewrites the insights pipeline from shallow keyword-matching to a deep, extensible feature extraction system that exhausts every computable signal from structured trace data. The heuristic layer alone now produces actionable reports — no LLM needed.

### What changed

**Phase A: 10-Extractor Pipeline** (`src/sagg/analytics/insights/extractors.py`)
- Registry-based architecture: each extractor is a class with `name`, `version`, `extract()`. Adding a new signal = write one class + append to `EXTRACTORS` + `--force` re-run
- Produces ~40 attributes per session vs ~15 in v1
- Extractors: ToolCallStats, ErrorAnalysis, Intervention, Timing, FilePattern, TokenUsage, ConversationFlow, OutcomeSignals, GoalClassification, Complexity
- Key new signals: per-tool error counts, error recovery rate, error clustering (early/middle/late), user intervention detection (post-error vs proactive), conversation pattern classification, satisfaction/frustration detection

**Phase B: DB Migration v4 to v5** (`src/sagg/storage/db.py`)
- Adds `facet_json TEXT` column to `session_facets` table
- Full extractor output stored as JSON — no schema migration needed when new extractors are added
- Existing typed columns remain for indexed SQL queries

**Phase C: HTML Report Generator** (`src/sagg/export/html_report.py`)
- Standalone HTML file with all CSS inline — no external dependencies
- Dark mode via `prefers-color-scheme`, mobile-responsive
- CSS bar charts for success rates and friction
- Copy buttons on suggestions via `navigator.clipboard`
- Sections: At a Glance, Tool Comparison, Friction Analysis, Suggestions, Trends, Project Areas, LLM Narrative (when available)

**Phase D: CLI Integration** (`src/sagg/cli.py`)
- `analyze-sessions` now uses v2 extractors by default (heuristic_v2)
- `insights --format html` generates and saves standalone HTML report
- `insights --format html -o custom.html` saves to custom path

### Tests
- **380 total tests passing** (88 new)
- 71 extractor tests covering all 10 extractors + pipeline
- 17 HTML report tests (structure, content, no external deps, dark mode, etc.)
- 3 new store tests for facet_json column
- Zero regressions in existing 292 tests

### What is next (separate PR)
- LLM map-reduce layer: batch facet JSONs (not raw transcripts) for cheaper, focused narrative generation
- Aggregator v2: uses full facet_json for richer cross-tool analysis

jameslcowan
body:
## Summary

Fixes #4422.

## Problem

`MCPServer.__aexit__()` checked `_running_count == 0` **outside** `_enter_lock`, while `__aenter__()` correctly performs its check **inside** the lock.

With `_running_count == 1` and two coroutines exiting concurrently:

1. Both coroutines read `_running_count == 1` and pass the guard
2. Both acquire the lock in turn and decrement
3. Final count: **-1**

This corrupts lifecycle state — a subsequent `__aenter__` sees `-1 != 0`, skips initialization, increments to 0, and proceeds with a closed client.

## Fix

Move the guard check inside the lock so the read and decrement are atomic:

```python
# Before
async def __aexit__(self, *args):
    if self._running_count == 0:          # outside lock ❌
        raise ValueError(...)
    async with self._enter_lock:
        self._running_count -= 1
        ...

# After
async def __aexit__(self, *args):
    async with self._enter_lock:
        if self._running_count == 0:      # inside lock ✅
            raise ValueError(...)
        self._running_count -= 1
        ...
```

## Changes

- `pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/mcp.py`: move guard inside lock (2-line change)
- `tests/test_mcp.py`: add `asyncio` import + regression test for concurrent exits

## Tests

```
tests/test_mcp.py::test_aexit_called_more_times_than_aenter PASSED
tests/test_mcp.py::test_aexit_concurrent_does_not_corrupt_running_count PASSED
```

body:
## What

Add `list_directory` — the 6th MCP tool in largefile.

Lists the contents of a directory with configurable recursion depth, hidden-file
filtering, and automatic ignore patterns for common noise directories
(`__pycache__`, `node_modules`, `.git`). Returns entry type, size in bytes, and
direct child count for each entry, plus truncation metadata when the result is
capped at `max_entries`.

## Why

`get_overview` and `search_content` are powerful once you know the path to the
file you care about. In large, unfamiliar codebases that knowledge isn't always
available upfront. `list_directory` fills the gap: an agent can discover the
project layout — packages, modules, config directories — before diving into
individual files, without needing any prior context about the repo structure.

This was listed as a high-priority item in the project roadmap and follows the
same design philosophy as the existing tools: read-only, composable, gracefully
bounded.

## Changes

| Area | What changed |
|---|---|
| `src/data_models.py` | New `DirectoryEntry` and `DirectoryListing` dataclasses |
| `src/config.py` | `LARGEFILE_MAX_DIR_ENTRIES` (default 200) and `LARGEFILE_IGNORED_DIR_PATTERNS` (default `__pycache__,node_modules,.git`) |
| `src/tools.py` | Private `_Counter` dataclass, `_collect_entries` recursive helper, and `list_directory` public tool |
| `src/mcp_schemas.py` | `ToolsModule` Protocol entry, `get_tool_schemas()` registration, `call_tool` branch |
| `docs/API.md` | New `### list_directory` section; overview table updated (5 → 6 tools) |
| `docs/configuration.md` | Two new env-var entries |
| `README.md` | Tool count and table updated |
| `tests/` | 14 unit tests (`tmp_path` fixtures) + 6 integration tests (real repo tree) |

## How it was tested

**Unit tests** — `tests/unit/test_tools_list_directory.py` (14 tests):
- Empty directory, single file, single subdir
- Dirs listed before files (sort order)
- `include_hidden=False` hides dot-entries; `include_hidden=True` shows them
- Default ignore patterns skip `__pycache__`, `node_modules`, `.git`
- `max_depth=1` does not recurse; `max_depth=2` includes one nested level
- Truncation: `max_entries=3` on a 10-file dir sets `truncated=True` and populates `truncated_at`
- Error paths return `{"error": ..., "suggestion": ...}` dicts (not raw exceptions)

**Integration tests** — `tests/integration/test_directory_workflows.py` (6 tests, real repo tree):
- `test_data/` root lists ≥5 language subdirs including `python`, `java`, `go`
- `python/` subdir contains at least one `.py` file with `size_bytes > 0`
- `java/` subdir contains `spring-application.java`
- Depth-2 scan of `test_data/` finds files inside language subdirs
- `src/` scan returns all known module files (`tools.py`, `config.py`, `data_models.py`)
- Non-existent path returns `{"error": ...}` dict

**Full suite:** 295 tests pass, 88% coverage — no regressions.

**Static analysis:** `ruff format --check`, `ruff check`, and `mypy src/` all clean.

**Manual MCP functional test** (via `largefile-dev` server against a real Spring Boot
codebase with 75 Java source files across 33 packages):

```
# Recursive depth=5 on src/main/java: 42 files, 33 dirs detected correctly
# Truncation to max_entries=10: truncated=True, truncated_at points to next file
# include_hidden=True: .gradle, .settings, .classpath, .project appear
# File path instead of dir: {"error": "File access failed: Not a directory..."}
```

- [x] `@handle_tool_errors` applied; error paths tested via dict check (not `pytest.raises`)

### Motivation

- Provide a runnable prototype to validate and update translated search terms for overseas sites by combining MT and LLM review.
- Reduce LLM cost with rule-based prefiltering, caching and frequency-based prioritization, and produce outputs for automated use and human review.

### Description

- Add a Python CLI `tool/validator.py` that loads two common CSV schemas, normalizes rows, calls Hunyuan-MT (local command or API), optionally calls an LLM for edge cases, and emits decisions per term. 
- Implement similarity-based rules, `should_trigger_llm` threshold, caching (`.validator_cache.json`), and decision outputs (`accept_old | replace_with_mt | human_review`) with scoring and ambiguity tags.

## Summary
- changed `ShepherdSpecialGoal.findTaskType` so `TaskType.BANNER` is only selected when both:
  - a banner is available (villager inventory/hand or chest), and
  - `findNearestPenTarget(world)` can resolve an unbannered pen target.
- this prevents entering the banner start flow when no valid pen can be targeted, which was causing repeated `shepherd_banner_start_no_pen_target` warnings.

## Root cause
The goal selected banner mode whenever a banner existed, even if every detected pen was already bannered (or otherwise not targetable). The failure was only discovered later in `start()`, producing the warning repeatedly on each retry cycle.

## Behavior after change
- if an unbannered valid pen exists, banner workflow still runs.
- if no unbannered pen exists, banner workflow is skipped (no repeated warning spam).
- shears and wheat-gather task selection remains unchanged in priority.

author: git-on-my-level
body:
## Summary
- fix Discord `/car newt` base-repo resolution to require a real manifest base repo id before creating a worktree
- add a fallback for legacy/stale worktree ids (for example `discord-car-wt-*`) that resolves the base repo via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`
- keep existing fast-path behavior when inferred base ids are already valid

## Root Cause
`/car newt` inferred `base_repo_id` from the bound worktree repo id. For legacy ids missing `worktree_of` metadata, inference could return a non-base id such as `discord-car`. That value was passed directly to `HubSupervisor.create_worktree`, which then failed with:

`Failed to create worktree: Base repo not found: discord-car`

Telegram appeared to work because it was bound to a repo/worktree whose metadata and id pattern still mapped cleanly to a base repo.

## Testing
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/integrations/discord/test_newt_base_repo_id.py`
- pre-commit hook suite on commit:
  - Discord contract guardrails
  - black / ruff / mypy / generated asset checks
  - full pytest (`1984 passed, 3 skipped`)

author: dcccrypto
body:
## PERC-170: Fix 3 Visual Regressions

Designer found 3 visual issues during 2:45 AM verification:

### 1. [P1] Hero gap at 1440px — ~350px black void below hero
**Root cause:** `ScrollReveal` used `IntersectionObserver` with `rootMargin: '0px 0px -60px 0px'` and `threshold: 0.08`. At 1440px viewports, the 'Built Different' stats section sat right at the fold edge — the 60px bottom margin clip prevented the observer from triggering, leaving the section at `opacity: 0`.

**Fix:**
- Reduced rootMargin to `-30px` and threshold to `0.05` for earlier triggering
- Added a 2-second safety timer that force-reveals any section where the observer hasn't fired (prevents invisible gaps at any viewport size)

### 2. [P2] Duplicate sticky nav at ~800px scroll
**Root cause:** `TickerBanner` had `z-50` (same as the sticky `Header`). As content scrolled, the TickerBanner rendered at the same z-layer as the Header, creating a visual duplicate. The Header also started with `bg-transparent`, allowing scrolling content to bleed through.

**Fix:**
- Lowered TickerBanner z-index from `z-50` → `z-40` 
- Header now uses `bg-[var(--bg)]/80 backdrop-blur-sm` when not scrolled (instead of fully transparent)

### 3. [P3] Architecture terminal — low contrast code block
**Root cause:** Terminal text in the 'No Permission Needed' card used `--text-dim` (`#2A2E3D`) — nearly invisible on the `--bg-elevated` (`#0F1018`) background.

**Fix:**
- Command line: `--text-muted` → `--text-secondary` (`#7A7F96`) — clearly readable
- Output lines: `--text-dim` → `--text-muted` (`#454B5F`) — subdued but visible

### Testing
- ✅ `pnpm build` — passes
- ✅ 521/521 unit tests pass (38 test files)
- 4 files changed, 29 insertions, 7 deletions

author: copilot
body:
Agents currently respond in complete isolation. The scratchpad pattern introduces opt-in sequential execution where each agent sees what prior agents said, enabling group conversation dynamics.

### Changes

- **`config/agents.py`** (new): `SCRATCHPAD_AGENT_ORDER` — execution order reflecting the film's emotional arc: Joy → Sadness → Fear → Disgust → Anger
- **`agents/personality_agents.py`**: `use_scratchpad: bool = False` on `MultiAgentSystem.__init__()`. When enabled, `get_responses()` iterates agents in order, accumulating lightweight context strings appended to the user message. Elapsed time is logged.
- **`tests/test_scratchpad.py`** (new): 15 tests covering ordering, context accumulation, parallel-mode preservation, @mention compat, and response format
- **`AGENTS.md`**: New Section 14 + updated orchestration docs and file map

### How it works

```python
system = MultiAgentSystem(use_scratchpad=True)
result = system.get_responses("What do you all think about pineapple on pizza?")
# Joy responds first (no scratchpad context)
# Sadness sees: [Joy already responded: 'Ooh, I love that! ✨']
# Fear sees both Joy and Sadness entries
# ...and so on
```

Context injection is a short bracketed string per prior agent — not a full history replay. When `use_scratchpad=False` (default), behavior is identical to the existing independent execution path.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> 
> ----
> 
> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>Inter-Agent Communication via Shared Scratchpad</issue_title>
> <issue_description>urrently all five personality agents respond in parallel and completely independently. None of them know what the others are saying. This misses a major opportunity: in the film, the emotions are constantly reacting to each other, arguing, and building off one another's ideas. That group dynamic is what makes Inside Out entertaining — and right now the system produces five isolated monologues instead.
> 
> **Design Pattern: Sequential Execution with Shared Scratchpad**
> 
> The scratchpad pattern is a coordination mechanism for multi-agent systems where agents need to be aware of each other's work. Instead of running fully in parallel, agents run in a defined order. Each agent's output is written to a shared scratchpad before the next agent runs, and the next agent receives the scratchpad as additional context.
> 
> The key design decisions are:
> 
> **Execution order** should reflect the emotional arc of the film: Joy → Sadness → Fear → Disgust → Anger. Joy responds first (she handles neutral queries by default), and subsequent agents receive her response as context framed as: *"Joy just said: '...' — now respond in YOUR voice, reacting to what Joy said if it's relevant."* This creates the appearance of a group conversation.
> 
> **Opt-in mode** is essential. The scratchpad approach is inherently sequential — each agent must wait for the previous one to finish — so it is slower than parallel execution. The original parallel mode should remain the default, with scratchpad mode enabled via a `use_scratchpad: bool` flag on `MultiAgentSystem`. Users who want faster responses keep the default; users who want richer inter-agent dynamics opt in.
> 
> **Context injection** should be lightweight. The scratchpad context passed to each agent should be a short, clearly labelled string appended to the user message — not a full conversation history. Something like: `"\n\n[Joy already responded: 'Ooh, that's so exciting! ✨']"` gives enough context without overwhelming the prompt.
> 
> **What needs to be done**
> 
> Add a `use_scratchpad: bool` parameter to `MultiAgentSystem.__init__()` (default `False`). When `True`, `get_responses()` should run agents sequentially in the configured order (define the order in `config/agents.py`) and pass each agent the accumulated scratchpad as context. When `False`, behaviour is unchanged from the current parallel implementation.
> 
> **Acceptance Criteria**
> - When `use_scratchpad=True`, agent responses demonstrate awareness of prior agents' outputs (validated by manual testing with prompts that activate 3+ agents).
> - Execution order is defined in `config/agents.py` and documented in `AGENTS.md`.
> - Total response time with scratchpad mode enabled is logged so the performance trade-off is visible.
> - The original parallel mode still works correctly when `use_scratchpad=False`.
> - Update AGENTS.md file with this changes 
> 
> **Files to change:** `agents/personality_agents.py` → `MultiAgentSystem.__init__()` and `get_responses()`, `config/agents.py` → new execution order config

author: gregorstocks
body:
## Summary

Closes the `mana-tapping-reeval` investigation issue. Analyzed 108 games with `harnessEpoch >= 10` using `scripts/analysis/mana_tapping.py`.

## Findings

### mana_plan vs auto_tap usage
- **mana_plan dominates**: 87% of mana payment actions (4,348 mana_plan vs 646 auto_tap)
- Overall **89% success rate** for mana_plan

### mana_plan success rate by model

**Strong (95%+):** GPT-5-nano (97%), GPT-5.2 (97%), GPT-5-mini (96%), Gemini-3-flash (96%), Claude Sonnet 4.5 (96%), O3 (95%)

**Moderate (65-90%):** Claude Opus 4.6 (90%), Gemini-3-pro (81%), Kimi-k2.5 (81%), Mimo-v2-flash (75%), Gemini-2.5-flash (68%), Gemini-2.5-pro (66%)

**Weak (<50%, should default to auto_tap):**
| Model | Success Rate |
|-------|-------------|
| grok-4-fast | 7% |
| llama-4-maverick | 20% |
| kimi-k2-0905 | 25% |
| deepseek-v3.2 | 29% |
| minimax-m2.1 | 41% |
| qwen3-235b | 48% |

### :N ability index syntax (dual lands)
- 13% of mana_plan entries use `:N` syntax (410/3,182)
- Heavy users: Gemini-3-flash (49%), Llama-4-maverick (50%), Grok-4-fast (33%)
- Non-users: GPT-5-mini (0%), GPT-5-nano (0%), Minimax (0%), Claude Haiku (0%)
- Most models have very low adoption — the feature works but isn't widely used

### Top failure reasons
1. Wrong action state — sending mana_plan when not in a casting context ("GAME_SELECT requires index=N")
2. Stale permanent IDs — referencing objects that aren't on the battlefield ("Object pN not found")
3. Sending both mana_plan and auto_tap simultaneously
4. Server timing issues ("No pending action after 10s wait")

### Recommendations
- **Keep mana_plan** — works excellently for the strongest models (OpenAI family, Anthropic family, Gemini-3-flash)
- **6 models should default to auto_tap**: deepseek-v3.2, grok-4-fast, kimi-k2-0905, llama-4-maverick, minimax-m2.1, qwen3-235b
- The `:N` syntax is functional but low adoption — may not be worth the complexity for most models
- Major error categories suggest tool description improvements could help weaker models

## Test plan
- [x] Ran `scripts/analysis/mana_tapping.py` on 108 epoch >= 10 games
- [x] Verified findings with detailed per-model error breakdowns

author: jaredlewiswechs
body:
## Summary
This PR introduces Ink, a new iOS chat application that leverages Apple's Foundation Models for on-device AI conversations. The app provides a persistent, privacy-focused chat interface with full conversation history management.

## Key Changes

### Core Architecture
- **InkEngine**: Main bridge to Apple's Foundation Models with streaming response support, session management, and automatic conversation title generation
- **SwiftData Models**: `Conversation` and `Message` models for persistent local storage with proper relationships and cascade deletion
- **Error Handling**: Custom `InkError` enum for model availability and generation failures

### User Interface
- **ConversationListView**: Sidebar showing all conversations grouped by date (Today, Yesterday, This Week, etc.) with search functionality
- **ConversationDetailView**: Main chat thread view with message display, real-time streaming responses, and auto-scrolling
- **Message Components**: 
  - `MessageBubble`: iMessage-style bubbles with different styling for user vs. assistant messages
  - `TypingIndicator`: Animated pulsing dots while AI is generating
  - `InputBar`: Text input field with send button, supporting multi-line input
- **SettingsView**: Configuration for system prompts, response style slider, conversation management, and export functionality
- **EmptyStateView**: Placeholder for iPad split view when no conversation is selected

### Utilities & Features
- **ContextWindow**: Token budget management for the 4K token context window with message selection algorithm
- **DateGrouping**: Conversation grouping by relative dates for organized sidebar display
- **Exporter**: JSON export of all conversations with metadata for sharing/backup
- **Availability Handling**: Graceful UI for devices without Apple Intelligence support

### Project Configuration
- Complete Xcode project setup with proper build phases, file references, and build settings
- Swift 6.0 with iOS 26.0 deployment target
- Foundation Models entitlement configuration
- Asset catalog with app icon and accent color support

## Notable Implementation Details
- All conversations stored locally on-device with no server communication
- Streaming responses displayed in real-time as they're generated
- Automatic context window management to fit within model limits
- System prompt customization per conversation
- Full conversation export capability for data portability

Here's a breakdown of the changes securely applied to the

Redesigned the "Public" / "Private" option switch to accurately reflect the Figma design.
Added a Megaphone icon for "Public" and a Lock icon for "Private".
The active state correctly updates the toggle to a distinctive style (white background, very subtle inner border styling for the circular icon wrapper), whereas the non-active state blends in perfectly as an outline variation with gray text.
Only one option is active at a time, governed by the form state's visibility toggle string property.

handleClear

"Create Event": Properly utilizes the filled Yellow #FFD233 shade and sports a disabled variant tracking the truth states of !formData.title.trim() or !formData.startDate.trim().
Disabled styles were adjusted precisely to Figma's reference: dropping standard interactive traits (opacity-50 cursor-not-allowed) rather than utilizing arbitrary dashed borders.
Submission fires 

handleSubmit()
 which console logs the entire payload formData for backend integration readiness.
4. Form State Management Architecture
Maintained the single parent useState object, <EventFormData>, containing all default initialized values, which is correctly tracking values concurrently.

author: copilot
body:
Restructures `app/` from flat layered directories (`Models/`, `Services/`, etc.) into a domain-driven layout under `app/Domains/`.

### Domain structure

```
app/Domains/
├── Shared/         → User, Tenant, Employee, Banner, Configuration, Enums, Fortify Actions
├── Finance/        → Transaction model/service/controller, CreateTransaction listener
├── Attendance/     → CheckInOut, Streak, CheckInOutService, MemberCheckedIn event
├── Membership/     → Membership, Package, events/listeners/notifications, console command
└── UserManagement/ → EmployeeService, AnalyticService, DashboardService, AuditService
```

### Changes

- **File moves + namespace updates**: All models, services, controllers, events, listeners, notifications, requests, enums, and console commands moved to their respective domain folders with updated namespaces
- **Cross-domain imports**: Added explicit `use` imports for all cross-domain model relationships (e.g., `User` → `Membership`, `CheckInOut`, `Streak`, `Transaction`; `Membership` → `User`, `Employee`)
- **Import updates project-wide**: Routes, providers, config (`auth.php`, `tenancy.php`), database (seeders, migrations, factories), Filament resources, middleware, blade views, and all tests
- **AdminPanelProvider**: Added `discoverResources` calls for each domain's potential Filament resource path
- **Command registration**: Uses `withCommands()` in `bootstrap/app.php` instead of `Artisan::load()` (which calls a protected `Kernel::load()` method in Laravel 12)
- **Cleanup**: Removed empty `app/Models`, `app/Services`, `app/Events`, `app/Listeners`, `app/Notifications`, `app/Console`, `app/Enums`, `app/Actions`, `app/Http/Requests`, `app/Http/Controllers/Admin`, `app/Http/Controllers/Member`

### Laravel 12 note

`Artisan::load()` does not work in Laravel 12 — it proxies to `Kernel::load()` which is protected. Domain console commands are registered via:

```php
// bootstrap/app.php
->withCommands([
    app_path('Domains/Membership/Console'),
])
```

All 55 domain classes verified autoloading correctly. All routes resolve to new controller namespaces.

author: windoliver
body:
## Summary

Closes #55.

Aligns `@koi/doctor` with the [OWASP Agentic Security Initiative Top 10 (Dec 2025)](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/agentic-ai/) by adding 5 new rules (total: 30), refactoring shared helpers, and hardening the runner.

**New rules added:**

| Rule ID | OWASP | Severity | What it checks |
|---|---|---|---|
| `supply-chain:forge-verification-disabled` | ASI04 | HIGH | `metadata.forge.verification` is absent or false |
| `code-execution:no-redaction-middleware` | ASI05 | MEDIUM | No `redaction` middleware when tools are configured |
| `cascading-failures:no-budget-limits` | ASI08 | MEDIUM | No `budget`/`pay` middleware or `metadata.maxCostUsd` |
| `rogue-agents:no-agent-monitor` | ASI10 | MEDIUM | Delegation enabled but no `agent-monitor` middleware |
| `insecure-delegation:no-a2a-auth` | ASI07 | HIGH | Delegation enabled but no `a2a-auth` middleware |

**Refactoring:**

- Extract `src/metadata.ts` → `getMetadataKey()` shared helper (removes inline type guards scattered across rule files)
- Rename `insecure-delegation.ts` → `inter-agent-comms.ts` via `git mv` (file name aligns with ASI07 spec; rule IDs are unchanged — non-breaking)
- Fix `runner.ts`: remove dead `.then()` on `Promise<never>`, fix O(n²) spread accumulation in `collectResults`, run advisory callback concurrently with rules via `Promise.all`
- Add `advisoryError?: string` to `DoctorReport` for non-fatal advisory feed failures

**Note on OWASP IDs:** The issue description used a draft numbering. The existing code already uses the correct Dec 2025 IDs (ASI01–ASI10). No renaming needed.

## Test plan

- [ ] `bun test packages/doctor` — all 269 tests pass, 0 failures
- [ ] `index.test.ts` — asserts exactly 30 rules, all unique names, all 5 categories, all 10 OWASP IDs
- [ ] `e2e.test.ts` — insecure manifest triggers findings across all 10 OWASP categories; `rulesApplied === 30`
- [ ] `metadata.test.ts` — 8 unit tests covering undefined input, absent key, and all value types
- [ ] `cascading-failures.test.ts`, `supply-chain.test.ts`, `code-execution.test.ts`, `rogue-agents.test.ts`, `inter-agent-comms.test.ts` — new rule tests included
- [ ] `integration.test.ts` — advisory error surface test passes with new `advisoryError` field
- [ ] `full-stack.e2e.test.ts` — gated on `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; secure manifest passes clean bill of health

body:
### Motivation
- Make the UI more legible by switching from retro pixel/monospace styling to a clean, readable sans-serif and by reducing high-contrast decorative elements.
- Darken and simplify background and surface colors to improve contrast and reduce visual noise.
- Remove grid lines from charts and decorative grid backgrounds to achieve a cleaner presentation.

### Description
- Replaced the pixel/monospace fonts with the `Inter` family and fallbacks and updated font usage site-wide for improved legibility in the UI.
- Updated theme variables (colors, muted/text contrast, and `--radius`) to a darker, calmer palette and softer radii for a cleaner modern look.
- Removed repeating/grid background decorations from the main content and simplified the background gradients for less visual noise.
- Adjusted header/logo/button typography and shadows to reduce aggressive styling and make controls easier to read.
- Disabled Chart.js grid lines and brightened axis tick colors (using `grid: { display: false }` and lighter tick colors) across trend, fair-value, and per-minute charts so charts appear cleaner on the dark background.
- Modified `static/index.html` to implement the above CSS and Chart.js option updates.

### Testing
- Ran `python -m py_compile server.py jre_analyzer/*.py` and the compile check completed successfully.
- Attempted an automated headless browser check to capture a screenshot, but navigation to the local dev server returned `ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE` in this environment (no successful screenshot captured).

author: phillipleblanc
body:
## Summary
- Handle a scheduler race where a `Completed` job event can arrive before terminal status is persisted.
- In `QueryHandle::fetch_completed_job_locations`, poll `get_job_status` briefly after `Completed` before failing.
- Treat transient `None` / `Queued` / `Running` states as retryable during this poll window; still fail immediately on `Failed`.

## Why
`cluster::in_memory_shuffle::test_in_memory_shuffle_multiple_executors` was flaky with:

`Failed to get job status: Job ... reported as completed but status is not successful`

This was caused by timing between completed-event emission and terminal status visibility.

## Validation
- `cargo test -p runtime --test integration test_in_memory_shuffle_multiple_executors -- --nocapture`
- Repeated loop run: **30/30 passes** after the fix (previously reproduced failure before fix).

Related CI failure examples:
- https://github.com/spiceai/spiceai/actions/runs/22428233285/job/64943097703
- https://github.com/spiceai/spiceai/actions/runs/22428937161/job/64945364458

author: openperf
body:
Fixes #27201

## Summary

When processing a Telegram reply context, `describeReplyTarget()` in `src/telegram/bot/helpers.ts` did not check if `replyLike.text` or `replyLike.caption` were strings before using them. In edge cases where the Telegram API returns a non-string value (e.g., an object), JavaScript's string coercion results in `[object Object]` appearing in the delivered message content.

This commit fixes the issue by adding a `typeof rawReplyText === "string"` guard to ensure that only string values are used. This prevents the `[object Object]` bug and aligns the reply context logic with existing safe patterns in the codebase.

## Changes

| File | What changed |
|---|---|
| `src/telegram/bot/helpers.ts` | Added a `typeof` check for `replyLike.text ?? replyLike.caption` in `describeReplyTarget()`. |
| `src/telegram/bot.ts` | Added a similar defensive `typeof` guard in `getTelegramSequentialKey()` for `msg.text ?? msg.caption`. |
| `src/telegram/bot/helpers.test.ts` | Added two new test cases to verify that non-string `text` and `caption` values are handled gracefully and do not produce `[object Object]`. |

author: scartill
body:
This PR improves the error handling in the NMEA parser. Previously, `iterate_nmea_file` swallowed all `ValueError` exceptions by just logging them, which made it difficult for callers to be strict about data quality.

### Changes:
- **`iterate_nmea_file`**:
    - Added a `strict: bool = False` parameter. When `True`, parsing errors raise a `ValueError` with contextual information (line number and content).
    - Switched to idiomatic `for line in f` iteration with `enumerate` for line numbering.
    - Explicitly catch `pynmea2.ParseError` along with `ValueError`.
    - Skips empty lines and strips whitespace.
- **`extract_sensor_data`**:
    - Added a check to ensure GGA messages were found before attempting to unpack the result of `zip(*iterate())`, preventing a cryptic `ValueError` when processing empty or invalid files.

### Verification:
- Created a verification script that mocks `pynmea2` and confirms that:
    - `strict=False` logs warnings and continues.
    - `strict=True` raises exceptions with line numbers.
    - `extract_sensor_data` handles empty data by raising a descriptive error.
- Verified compatibility with `convert_to_fvc`.

body:
### Motivation
- Enable users to freely rearrange flow labels (chips) and have the corresponding card flow move with the label while keeping the existing long-press merge behavior intact.

### Description
- Updated `app/src/main/java/com/example/timescapedemo/MainActivity.kt` to add a dedicated reorder drag channel `FLOW_REORDER_DRAG_LABEL` and an `activeFlowReorderDragId` state variable to track reorder drags.
- Enhanced the chip rendering and drag listener to recognize reorder drags alongside existing merge and card-move drags, and to route `DROP` events to `moveFlow` for reordering.
- Added touch-slop based touch detection on chips to start reorder drags (using `ViewConfiguration.scaledTouchSlop` and `MotionEvent` + `hypot`) so a drag only starts after a deliberate pointer move, while preserving the long-press merge start.

## Summary

Fixes a regression where pressing F12 (or any F-key) was recorded as **fn F12** instead of just **F12**, even when the user had not physically pressed the Fn key.

- macOS automatically sets the `maskSecondaryFn` flag on CGEvents for function key presses when "Use F1–F12 as standard function keys" is enabled in System Settings — the app was incorrectly treating this as an explicit Fn modifier
- Strip `maskSecondaryFn` during **capture** so newly recorded function key hotkeys are stored cleanly
- Strip it during **matching** (on both stored flags and incoming event flags) so existing configs previously saved as "fn F12" continue to fire correctly
- Strip it in the Flutter **display** function so old stored configs no longer show "fn F12" in the UI

Closes https://github.com/Matinrahimik/open_yapper/issues/13

## Files changed

- `macos/Runner/HotkeyManager.swift` — `isFunctionKeyCode()` helper, capture fix, `HotkeySpec.matches` fix

body:
### Motivation

- Provide a single, scheduled pipeline that runs the daily data/analytics steps, a gated biweekly learning flow for weight updates, and an end-of-season workflow, while making runs resilient to single-step failures. 
- Add a small operational check (`cron_check.py`) so operators can quickly inspect last-run health and whether the biweekly weight-update threshold is met.

### Description

- Added `.github/workflows/cbb_pipeline.yml` implementing three tiers (DAILY @ 09:00 UTC, BIWEEKLY @ 10:00 UTC on 1st/15th, END_OF_SEASON @ 10:00 UTC on Apr 10) with manual `workflow_dispatch` tier selection and `DATA_DIR` + `TZ` environment wiring. 
- Each tier runs steps using a `run_step` wrapper that records per-step status to `data/pipeline_step_runs.csv`, writes errors to `data/pipeline_errors.log`, and continues executing subsequent steps even if a step fails. 
- BIWEEKLY tier includes a prerequisite check (Python snippet) that loads `data/predictions_graded.csv` and `data/active_weights.json`, computes graded games since `last_weight_update`, and only proceeds if >= 200 graded games; otherwise it logs the skip reason. 
- END_OF_SEASON tier runs full validation/optimization/deploy steps and archives `data/results_log.csv` to `data/archive/results_log_{year}.csv` when present. 
- Added `cron_check.py`, a small CLI that reports last successful run time per step, an `active_weights.json` summary, days since last weight update, graded games since last update, and whether the 200-game biweekly threshold is met.

### Testing

- Ran `python cron_check.py` locally and it executed (exit 0), printing the health summary and gracefully reporting missing `active_weights.json` and zero graded games in the local test state. 
- Verified `cron_check.py` is syntactically valid with `python -m py_compile cron_check.py` (exit 0).

author: daw25pinescript
body:
## Summary

Introduces the **Trade Senate Protocol** — a deterministic deliberation system that aggregates three independent analyst AI outputs (Technical, Macro, Risk) into a single structured trade decision with confidence scoring, hard-gate vetoes, and conditional trade plans.

## Key Changes

- **senateArbiter.js** (627 lines)
  - Core deliberation engine with 9-step decision pipeline
  - Procedural validation of analyst outputs against required schema
  - Quorum detection (2+ vote majority) with conflict resolution via conditional triggers
  - Evidence ledger with 4-rule weighting system (HTF bias, close-based confirmation, confluence, freshness)
  - Hard-gate veto system: Invalidation Gate, R:R Gate, Volatility Gate, Chop Gate, News Gate, Setup Quality Gate
  - Deterministic confidence scoring (0–100) based on confluences, conflicts, regime, and entry quality
  - Structured order builder producing Plan A (primary) and Plan B (conditional) with entry/invalidation/TP/management rules
  - Dissent synthesis capturing minority positions and failure conditions

- **senateArbiter.test.js** (438 lines)
  - 10 comprehensive test cases covering all acceptance criteria
  - Tests for procedural failures, quorum logic, hard gates, confidence scoring, and order generation
  - Fixtures for building valid analyst objects with configurable overrides
  - Node.js native test runner (no external test framework)

- **arbiterPanel.js** (310 lines)
  - UI renderer for senate decision output
  - Collapsible sections for docket, motions, evidence ledger, confidence breakdown, trade plans, and dissent
  - Colour-coded ruling badges (green=TRADE, amber=CONDITIONAL, red=NO_TRADE)
  - Evidence weight visualization with deciding rules
  - Plan A/B card layout with entry/invalidation/TP/management details

- **senate_arbiter_schema.json** (217 lines)
  - JSON Schema v2020-12 canonical output specification
  - Defines all required fields, enums, and nested structures
  - Documents the complete decision object shape for integration

- **promptGenerator.js** (142 lines)
  - Analyst prompt template generator ensuring consistent JSON output shape
  - Role-specific instructions for Technical, Macro, and Risk analysts
  - Embeds required output schema directly in prompts to guarantee compliance

- **main.js** (modified)
  - Integrated Senate Arbiter into main application
  - Added `runSenateArb()` handler to parse analyst JSON and invoke deliberation
  - Wired UI panel initialization and rendering

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Pure function design**: senateArbiter.js has no DOM access, no fetch calls, no side effects — all logic is deterministic and testable
- **Conflict resolution**: Direction disagreements (Long vs Short) are automatically resolved if the dissenting analyst provides conditional language in their alternative scenario
- **Evidence weighting**: Applies four independent rules (HTF bias +3, close-based +2, confluence +2 per extra analyst, freshness +1) with full rule attribution
- **Hard gates run in order**: Invalidation Gate executes before R:R Gate because missing invalidation is the root cause of uncomputable R:R
- **Confidence formula**: Base 50 + (confluences × 10, max +30) − (conflict × 15) − (choppy/ranging × 10) − (anticipation without confirmation × 10)
- **Conditional triggers**: Plan B activates only if a resolvable conflict exists and dissenting analyst provides conditional language (if/when/once/trigger/break/retest/confirm/above/below/close)

## Summary

Three fixes for `props` LLM request logging and model routing:

**1. Fix crash in LLM requests viewer (`runs.py`)**

`GET /api/runs/<id>/llm-requests` crashed with Pydantic `ValidationError` when any
request had an error response body (e.g. `{"error": {"message": "model not found"}}`).
`ResponsesResult` requires `id`; error responses don't have it.

Fix: `model_validator(mode="before")` in `LLMRequestInfo` detects error bodies (dicts
without `id`) and moves them to a new `response_error_body` field.

**2. Display error response bodies in frontend**

`LLMRequestViewer.svelte` previously only showed `req.error` (the HTTP status string).
Now also renders `response_error_body` as formatted JSON so the actual upstream error
message is visible.

**3. Fix model metadata sync missing content changes (`model_metadata.py`)**

`sync_model_metadata_with_session` had a count-based fast path: if DB model count ==
source count, skip the full sync. Changing `upstream_model` on an existing model
(without adding/removing models) was silently ignored.

For `gpt-oss-20b-128k`, the DB had `upstream_model=NULL`, so the LLM proxy sent the
alias name directly to Ollama instead of `gpt-oss:20b`, causing "model not found" errors.

Fix: remove the fast path; always do the full merge sync on startup.
Test: `test_model_metadata_sync.py` is a regression test for the fast-path bug.

- [ ] After pod restart, `gpt-oss-20b-128k` routes to Ollama as `gpt-oss:20b`

author: sam-at-luther
body:
## Summary

- Make `repl.RunEnv` extensible with 6 new functional options (`WithLineHandler`, `WithEvalFunc`, `WithCompleter`, `WithPromptFunc`, `WithInterruptFunc`, `WithDoneCh`) so the debug REPL layers on top without duplicating readline, parsing, or error rendering
- Add new `lisp/x/debugger/debugrepl/` package providing a full GDB-style CLI debugger with step/next/out/continue, breakpoints, backtrace, locals, print, and source context display
- Wire `elps debug --repl` flag to launch the CLI debug REPL instead of the DAP server
- Add `RemoveByID` to `BreakpointStore` for the `delete N` debug command

## Design

The debug REPL uses the same two-goroutine concurrency model as DAP: an eval goroutine runs `env.LoadFile()` (blocking in `WaitIfPaused` when paused), while the REPL goroutine reads commands via readline and dispatches to the engine. Commands like `continue`/`step`/`next` unblock the eval goroutine and wait on a `pausedCh` channel for the next stop event.

All readline, parsing, tokenization, and error rendering is reused from `repl.RunEnv` via the new hooks — the debugrepl package only handles command dispatch and display.

### Debug commands
| Command | Alias | Description |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| `continue` | `c` | Resume execution |
| `step` | `s` | Step into next expression |
| `next` | `n` | Step over (same depth) |
| `out` | `o` | Step out of current function |
| `break F:L [C]` | `b` | Set breakpoint at file:line with optional condition |
| `delete N` | `d` | Remove breakpoint by ID |
| `breakpoints` | `bl` | List all breakpoints |
| `backtrace` | `bt` | Show call stack |
| `locals` | `l` | Show local variables |
| `print EXPR` | `p` | Evaluate and print expression |
| `where` | `w` | Show source context |
| `quit` | `q` | End debug session |
| `help` | `h` | Show help |

Empty input repeats the last command (GDB convention). Non-command input is evaluated as Lisp in the paused scope.

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `repl/repl.go` | Add 6 config fields + Option constructors + hook usage in RunEnv |
| `lisp/x/debugger/breakpoint.go` | Add `RemoveByID(id int) bool` |
| `lisp/x/debugger/breakpoint_test.go` | Add `TestBreakpointStore_RemoveByID` |
| `lisp/x/debugger/debugrepl/repl.go` | **New.** Debug REPL core, command dispatch |
| `lisp/x/debugger/debugrepl/display.go` | **New.** Source context, backtrace, locals display |
| `lisp/x/debugger/debugrepl/complete.go` | **New.** Debug-aware readline completer |
| `lisp/x/debugger/debugrepl/repl_test.go` | **New.** 25 tests: unit + integration with piped stdin |
| `cmd/debug.go` | Add `--repl` flag, branch to debugrepl |

## Test plan

- [x] `make test` — all existing tests pass (repl options are additive, defaults unchanged)
- [x] `go test ./lisp/x/debugger/debugrepl/...` — 25 new tests pass
- [x] `go test ./lisp/x/debugger/...` — breakpoint tests pass including new RemoveByID
- [x] `make static-checks` — golangci-lint clean (0 issues)
- [x] Integration tests exercise full two-goroutine lifecycle: stop-on-entry, step, continue, break, print, locals, where, backtrace, quit
- [x] QA professor review: PASS on breakpoint_test.go, NEEDS WORK items addressed on debugrepl tests
- [x] Security review: no actionable findings for a local CLI tool
- [ ] Manual: `./elps debug --repl examples/hello.lisp` → pauses on entry, accepts commands
- [ ] Manual: `elps debug` (DAP mode, no `--repl`) still works as before

## Summary

bfcache復元時のセッション復帰を `router.refresh()` から `window.location.reload()` に変更。

## 問題

`router.refresh()` による RSC リクエストが iOS Safari で cookies を正しく付与できず、ミドルウェアがセッションなしと判断して `/login` へリダイレクトしていた。ログ分析から 50ms 以内にリダイレクトが発生しており、debounce (200ms) より速いことからも `router.refresh()` とは別の原因だと確認。

## 変更内容

- `pageshow(persisted=true)` のみ監視（bfcache 復元の確実な検知）
- `window.location.reload()` で完全なブラウザナビゲーションを実施
  - cookies が確実に付与される
  - ミドルウェアが正しくセッションをリフレッシュできる
- `visibilitychange` / `focus` ハンドラを削除（トークン競合の原因）
